question: Does the PDF comparison use normal KLQR, what causes its steady offset, and what happens after fresh unforced training from the PDF IC?
core_changes: None. New case-only C++ clients, jobs, metrics and Viewer figure assembly. All scientific fitting, simulation, control and validation use installed native services.

reference.qualification: The comparison is against our numerical reproduction of the supplied polynomial, not digitized numerical PDF data. The PDF does not fully specify its training settings or controller implementation.

training.duration_assumption: 25 nondimensional time units follows the documented RPE baseline; the PDF does not state a training duration.
training.solver: Native BDF, rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-11, maximum internal step 0.001
training.physics: Exactly the supplied PDF physics, including zero vapor pressure and viscosity 0.001 Pa s; normal DynSysLab nondimensionalization

fit.hdmd: Radius observable; 20000 by 2000 Hankel pair; stride 1; projected modes; full tolerance-selected rank; absolute SVD tolerance 1e-10; terminal-amplitude energy sort
fit.sindy: All 101 rates fitted as total-degree-four polynomials in raw (r,v), 14 nonconstant features, no state normalization, threshold 1e-6, one threshold pass, exact unforced RHS derivatives, conjugate reuse, coefficient-first archives
fit.coefficient_normalization: Unit Euclidean coefficient norm; both supplied and raw newly fitted polynomials have norm 1
fit.selection: The stable 5<Im(lambda)<7 band contains two positive-frequency candidates. First selected the smaller 0..25 anchored free-training error (index 4), then also controlled with the slower candidate (index 2) as a comparison. No control outcome was used for the first selection.
fit.mode_index_warning: Local zero-based indices 2 and 4 are NOT the PDF's phi_2 and phi_13 labels. In particular the PDF phi_2 has a different frequency near 28.1.

controller.implementation: native/src/LQR.cpp:43, KoopmanLQRController::value; invoked through ordinary workflow ControlFactory
controller.law: u=-K(x)*(split(psi(x))-split(psi(target))); continuous CARE recomputed from A, exact analytic B_psi(x), Q, R at each RHS evaluation
controller.Q_coordinates: Re(psi), Im(psi), NOT r and v
controller.extras: No feedforward, integral action, control caps, control-map regression, or latent-history coordinates

steady_offset_diagnosis.primary_cause: The feedback-only law vanishes at zero lifted tracking error, but the target is not an unforced equilibrium. Nonzero error is therefore needed to generate its holding pressure.
steady_offset_diagnosis.secondary_factors: Polynomial extrapolation and approximation error, eigenfunction phase/normalization, and the resulting effective feedback gains affect the size of the offset and transients. The target radius 1.3 is beyond the training maximum 1.2.
steady_offset_diagnosis.not_the_cause: No regressed B_psi or echo-history delay is involved. Numerical refinement is far smaller than the observed offsets.
steady_offset_diagnosis.recommendation: A separately authorized next experiment should regulate around the feasible state-input pair (target,u_star), or assess integral action. Standardize eigenfunction gauge and transform Q consistently when comparing representations. Do not equate a lower final tracking error with a better Koopman approximation.

gauge_diagnostic.description: Auxiliary only, not the primary new fit: multiply the faster polynomial by the least-squares complex coefficient-alignment scalar against the supplied polynomial. This changes no relative semigroup errors, but changes the objective under fixed numerical Q.
gauge_diagnostic.covariance_rule: For z_prime=T*z, equivalent weights are Q_prime=T^(-T)*Q*T^(-1); copying numerical Q unchanged does not preserve the cost.
gauge_diagnostic.not_claimed: This is not a new fit, a better eigenfunction, or an appropriate gauge convention to adopt globally.

limitations: This is a fresh standard-pipeline experiment, not exact reconstruction of undocumented PDF training settings.
All reported free-trajectory metrics here are in-sample diagnostics, not independent held-out certification.
A single spiral does not establish global eigenfunction validity or accuracy beyond its observed region.
The idealized peak input commands are large; no actuator limits or laboratory feasibility are established.
heavy_assets: Local ignored archives and PNGs only; source and metadata contain pointers. No commit or publication performed.
